Product Design Director - Patient (x/f/m)

The opportunity

Doctolib is a mission-driven healthcare technology company, founded in Paris in 2013. Today, nearly 3,000 people work across Europe to transform the way healthcare is delivered and experienced.

More than 500,000 healthcare professionals use Doctolib’s solutions, and the patient app is used by approximately 90 million people across Europe.

For patients, Doctolib began as a simple way to find a healthcare professional and book an appointment. We are now building something much more ambitious: an AI-powered Health Companion that helps people navigate care, understand their health and take the right next step throughout their health journey.

This means moving beyond a primarily transactional product towards an experience that supports patients before, during and after care, through access to care, health information, patient data, messaging, recommendations, care plans and AI-powered assistance.

We are looking for a Product Design Director to help define what this next generation of patient experience should look and feel like.

What you will build and lead

As Product Design Director, Patient, you will own the design vision and quality bar for Doctolib’s patient experience. You will report to our VP Design and work closely with the Product, Engineering, Medical, Data and Business leadership teams. 

Your scope will cover the full patient journey, including:

  • access to care, search and booking;

  • patient messaging and teleconsultation;

  • the Patient Health Record and patient context;

  • the app homepage and daily health experience;

  • health content and prevention;

  • recommendations, reminders and care plans;

  • new patient services and subscription experiences;

  • conversational and AI-powered experiences.

The current team includes six Senior Product Designers and one Senior Content Designer. You will lead, coach and develop this team while shaping the organisation and operating model needed to support the next phase of the Patient product.

Your mandate

You will:

  • Define and drive the design vision for the Patient stream, from a high-traffic booking experience to a trusted Health Companion used throughout the health journey.

  • Bridge two equally important challenges: continuing to improve the core access-to-care experience while creating new reasons for patients to return beyond booking.

  • Raise the quality bar for product design, interaction design and content across the patient experience.

  • Stay close enough to the product and the craft to make high-quality design decisions, not only set direction from a distance.

  • Shape AI-native experiences that are clear, useful and trustworthy, including recommendations, conversational interfaces and next-best actions.

  • Establish strong design principles for transparency, explainability, uncertainty, user control and safe escalation in a healthcare context.

  • Build a high-performing design organisation, including hiring, coaching, talent development and second-line leadership.

  • Create effective ways of working across Design, Product, Engineering, Medical, Data and Business.

  • Help scale a coherent experience across countries, languages and different healthcare contexts.

  • Connect design decisions to user behaviour, product outcomes and business impact.

What success looks like

In your first year, you will have:

  • established a clear and compelling design vision for the Patient stream;

  • raised the quality bar across both core access-to-care journeys and newer Health Companion experiences;

  • helped define a coherent interaction model for AI-powered patient experiences;

  • strengthened collaboration between Design, Product, Engineering and Medical;

  • developed a clear operating model and growth plan for the Patient Design organisation;

  • helped Doctolib increase the value and relevance of the patient experience beyond appointment booking.

What we are looking for

You are likely to bring:

  • Significant experience leading Product Design, 10+ years in product design including 3+ years in people leadership..

  • Experience in a consumer product organisation, ideally one used by millions of people.

  • A track record of designing and scaling products across multiple markets, with an understanding of localisation, cultural differences and the balance between global consistency and local relevance.

  • Experience managing at least five Product Designers, ideally a larger organisation including senior individual contributors and managers.

  • Strong product design craft and creative judgement. You can recognise excellent work, make difficult quality trade-offs and stay close enough to the details to raise the standard of the product.

  • Experience connecting design choices to measurable outcomes such as adoption, conversion, engagement, retention, satisfaction or user behaviour.

  • A strong and practical understanding of AI-native product experiences. You have thought deeply about how AI changes interaction design, user expectations, trust, transparency and control.

  • Experience designing with uncertainty, recommendations, personalisation or conversational interfaces is highly relevant.

  • The ability to operate across complex products and stakeholders, while maintaining clarity and momentum.

  • A concise and compelling communication style. You can articulate a clear point of view, align senior stakeholders and inspire teams to move in a new direction.

  • Experience in healthcare or another regulated, trust-sensitive environment is valuable, but healthcare experience is not required. What matters is your respect for domain expertise and your ability to design responsibly in high-stakes contexts.

  • Fluency in English. French or German would be a strong plus.

  • A working style aligned with the Doctolib Playbook: User First, Medical Expertise, Forefront of Innovation, Bold, Drive, Passion, Humility.

Why Doctolib, why now?

Doctolib gives you the opportunity to work on a consumer product with significant reach, strong European scale and a mission that matters.

The patient product already has a large and engaged audience. The next challenge is to make the experience more useful, more contextual and more present in people’s everyday health journeys.

You will join at a defining moment:

  • Doctolib is moving from appointment booking towards continuous health support.

  • AI is becoming a core part of the product experience, not an isolated feature.

  • The Patient Design organisation is being strengthened and reshaped.

  • The product must work across multiple European countries, languages and healthcare systems.

  • The design foundations for the next chapter are still being built.

This is an opportunity to shape a new category at the intersection of consumer product design, healthcare and AI, and to define how people will discover, understand and manage their health in the future.

Set a new pulse for healthcare!

 

We are looking for a Lead Product Manager to join the Patient Profile team in the Patient domain.

Your mission will be to make the patient health record complete, accurate and current enough that everything else we build can act on it, the health recommendations, care plans and assistant experiences that help people take their health into their own hands. You will work in a feature team developing the Patient Health Record, health trackers, patient account and online identity, contributing directly to the quality of the medical support we provide to both patients and practitioners. 

A patient record is built from four channels: what patients enter themselves, what they share when preparing a consultation, what we retrieve from health professionals' systems, and what they connect from third-party sources such as Apple Health, Google Health Connect and national health record services. Three of those channels belong to teams you will not manage. You will own the outcome across all four, the most leveraged place to sit in a health platform, and only reachable through other people.

You will also work inside a hard regulatory perimeter: health data, GDPR, consent by design. 

 

What you'll do

Your responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Own the end-to-end patient data collection programme across every channel a patient record is built from, and be accountable for the result across all four

  • Define what a useful record actually means for the teams that depend on it, make that definition measurable, and instrument it rather than inheriting a dashboard

  • Partner with the channel-owning teams inside and outside the group: set the inter-team contracts, agree how each channel contributes, and arbitrate collection priorities

  • Own record quality and freshness rather than volume, alongside health data storage consent, patient account and online identity

  • Ship the layers that serve this data to the rest of the product: the patient feature store, the patient context service and the Patient Health Record feature

  • Lead the Patient Profile team's roadmap and delivery, from PHR (patient health record) and trackers through to the feature store and context service

 

Who you are

quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app.

quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end.

Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll.

The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters.

Where this is going

Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either.

That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience.

One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy.

Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled.

Why this role exists

Today, quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with.

What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards.

That is the opening.

How we work

We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing.

We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way.

And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high.

Tasks

What you will own

Everything on the screen:

    We sell a mix of insurance products to small businesses (SME's) in the Netherlands, Germany and France, and we are in the process of scaling into more markets.

Most insurers throw people and process at that complexity - one-off integrations, workarounds on workarounds. We're building it differently: our insurance platform is where we consolidate that complexity, so that launching a new product or market becomes a configuration exercise rather than a rebuild.

    Insify is a high-growth scale-up backed by more than €40M from investors like Accel, Munich Re Ventures, and Formula 1 champion Nico Rosberg. In five years we've expanded from the Netherlands into France and Germany. Our mission: become the European leader in AI-powered SME insurance.


    About the role

    You would join the Shop team, responsible for everything that happens after a small business buys a policy from us. You would help shape how the platform handles the next product and the next country, on a system already carrying live policies and real customers.

    The team owns end-to-end policy lifecycle management (mid-term adjustments, automated renewals, cancellations, and payment flows) alongside the backoffice tooling that gives our operations and support teams full visibility and control.     Company Overview

    Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

    Company Operating Rhythm

    At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

    Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

    Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

    The Opportunity

    Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone.


    The Role

    As a Member of the Research Staff, you will pioneer the development of Latent Space Models (LSMs), a new approach that aims to solve the fundamental data, scale, and cost challenges associated with building robust, contextualized voice AI. Your research will focus on solving one or more of the following problems:

    • Build next-generation neural audio codecs that achieve extreme, low bit-rate compression and high fidelity reconstruction across a world-scale corpus of general audio.

    • Pioneer steerable generative models that can synthesize the full diversity of human speech from the codec latent representation, from casual conversation to highly emotional expression to complex multi-speaker scenarios with environmental noise and overlapping speech.

    • Develop embedding systems that cleanly factorize the codec latent space into interpretable dimensions of speaker, content, style, environment, and channel effects -- enabling precise control over each aspect and the ability to massively amplify an existing seed dataset through “latent recombination”.

    • Leverage latent recombination to generate synthetic audio data at previously impossible scales, unlocking joint model and data scaling paradigms for audio.  Endeavor to train multimodal speech-to-speech systems that can 1) understand any human irrespective of their demographics, state, or environment and 2) produce empathic, human-like responses that achieve conversational or task-oriented objectives.   

    • Design model architectures, training schemes, and inference algorithms that are adapted for hardware at the bare metal enabling cost efficient training on billion-hour datasets and powering real-time inference for hundreds of millions of concurrent conversations.

    The Challenge

    We are seeking researchers who:

    • See "unsolved" problems as opportunities to pioneer entirely new approaches

    • Can identify the one critical experiment that will validate or kill an idea in days, not months

    • Have the vision to scale successful proofs-of-concept 100x

    • Are obsessed with using AI to automate and amplify your own impact

This role demands obsession with the problems, creativity in approach, and relentless drive toward elegant, scalable solutions. The technical challenges are immense, but the potential impact is transformative.

    • Strong mathematical foundation in statistical learning theory, particularly in areas relevant to self-supervised and multimodal learning

    • Deep expertise in foundation model architectures, with an understanding of how to scale training across multiple modalities

    • Proven ability to bridge theory and practice—someone who can both derive novel mathematical formulations and implement them efficiently

    • History of open-source contributions or research publications that have advanced the state of the art in speech/language AI


    Ideal Researcher Profile

    An ideal researcher, as evidenced by the recurring themes across these foundational papers, excels in five key areas: (1) Statistical & Mathematical Foundations, (2) Algorithmic Innovation & Implementation, (3) Data-Driven & Scalable Systems, (4) Hardware & Systems Understanding, and (5) Rigorous Experimental Design. Below is a synthesis of how each paper highlights these qualities, with references illustrating why they matter for building robust, impactful deep learning models.



    1. Statistical & Mathematical Foundations

    Mastery of Core Concepts

    Many papers, like Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models and Neural Discrete Representation Learning (VQ-VAE), reflect the importance of power-law analyses, derivation of novel losses, or adaptation of fundamental equations (e.g., in VQ-VAE's commitment loss or rectified flows in Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers). Such mathematical grounding clarifies why models converge or suffer collapse.

    Combining Existing Theories in Novel Ways

    Papers such as Moshi (combining text modeling, audio codecs, and hierarchical generative modeling) and Finite Scalar Quantization (FSQ's adaptation of classic scalar quantization to replace vector-quantized representations) show how reusing but reimagining known techniques can yield breakthroughs. Many references (e.g., the structured state-space duality in Transformers are SSMs) underscore how unifying previously separate research lines can reveal powerful algorithmic or theoretical insights.

    Logical Reasoning and Assumption Testing

    Across all papers—particularly in the problem statements of Whisper or Rectified Flow Transformers—the authors present assumptions (e.g., "scaling data leads to zero-shot robustness" or "straight-line noise injection improves sample efficiency") and systematically verify them with thorough empirical results. An ideal researcher similarly grounds new ideas in well-formed, testable hypotheses.


    2. Algorithmic Innovation & Implementation

    Creative Solutions to Known Bottlenecks

    Each paper puts forth a unique algorithmic contribution—Rectified Flow Transformers redefines standard diffusion paths, FSQ proposes simpler scalar quantizations contrasted with VQ, phi-3 mini relies on curated data and blocksparse attention, and Mamba-2 merges SSM speed with attention concepts.

    Turning Theory into Practice

    Whether it's the direct preference optimization (DPO) for alignment in phi-3 or the residual vector quantization in SoundStream, these works show that bridging design insights with implementable prototypes is essential.

    Clear Impact Through Prototypes & Open-Source

    Many references (Whisper, neural discrete representation learning, Mamba-2) highlight releasing code or pretrained models, enabling the broader community to replicate and build upon new methods. This premise of collaboration fosters faster progress.


    3. Data-Driven & Scalable Systems

    Emphasis on Large-Scale Data and Efficient Pipelines

    Papers such as Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision (Whisper) and BASE TTS demonstrate that collecting and processing hundreds of thousands of hours of real-world audio can unlock new capabilities in zero-shot or low-resource domains. Meanwhile, phi-3 Technical Report shows that filtering and curating data at scale (e.g., "data optimal regime") can yield high performance even in smaller models.

    Strategic Use of Data for Staged Training

    A recurring strategy is to vary sources of data or the order of tasks. Whisper trains on multilingual tasks, BASE TTS uses subsets/stages for pretraining on speech tokens, and phi-3 deploys multiple training phases (web data, then synthetic data). This systematic approach to data underscores how an ideal researcher designs training curricula and data filtering protocols for maximum performance.


    4. Hardware & Systems Understanding

    Efficient Implementations at Scale

    Many works illustrate how researchers tune architectures for modern accelerators: the In-Datacenter TPU paper exemplifies domain-specific hardware design for dense matrix multiplications, while phi-3 leverages blocksparse attention and custom Triton kernels to run advanced LLMs on resource-limited devices.

    Real-Time & On-Device Constraints

    SoundStream shows how to compress audio in real time on a smartphone CPU, demonstrating that knowledge of hardware constraints (latency, limited memory) drives design choices. Similarly, Moshi's low-latency streaming TTS and phi-3-mini's phone-based inference highlight that an ideal researcher must adapt algorithms to resource limits while maintaining robustness.

    Architectural & Optimization Details

    Papers like Mamba-2 in Transformers are SSMs and the In-Datacenter TPU work show how exploiting specialized matrix decomposition, custom memory hierarchies, or quantization approaches can lead to breakthroughs in speed or energy efficiency.


    5. Rigorous Experimental Design

    Controlled Comparisons & Ablations

    Nearly all papers—Whisper, FSQ, Mamba-2, BASE TTS—use systematic ablations to isolate the impact of individual components (e.g., ablation on vector-quantization vs. scalar quantization in FSQ, or size of codebooks in VQ-VAEs). This approach reveals which design decisions truly matter.

    Multifold Evaluation Metrics

    From MUSHRA listening tests (SoundStream, BASE TTS) to FID in image synthesis (Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers, FSQ) to perplexity or zero-shot generalization in language (phi-3, Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models), the works demonstrate the value of comprehensive, carefully chosen metrics.

    Stress Tests & Edge Cases

    Whisper's out-of-distribution speech benchmarks, SoundStream's evaluation on speech + music, or Mamba-2's performance on multi-query associative recall demonstrate the importance of specialized challenge sets. Researchers who craft or adopt rigorous benchmarks and "red-team" their models (as in phi-3 safety alignment) are better prepared to address real-world complexities.



    Summary

    Overall, an ideal researcher in deep learning consistently demonstrates:

    • A solid grounding in theoretical and statistical principles

    • A talent for proposing and validating new algorithmic solutions

    • The capacity to orchestrate data pipelines that scale and reflect real-world diversity

    • Awareness of hardware constraints and system-level trade-offs for efficiency

    • Thorough and transparent experimental practices

    These qualities surface across research on speech (Whisper, BASE TTS), language modeling (Scaling Laws, phi-3), specialized hardware (TPU, Transformers are SSMs), and new representation methods (VQ-VAE, FSQ, SoundStream). By balancing these attributes—rigorous math, innovative algorithms, large-scale data engineering, hardware-savvy optimizations, and reproducible experimentation—researchers can produce impactful, trustworthy advancements in foundational deep learning.

    • Full attack-surface map. Build and maintain a living inventory of everything we run: internal apps, cloud, code repos, and every SaaS tool and integration (CRM, telephony, community, payments, data providers). Know what connects to what, who has access, and what is logged.

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced Digital Marketing Specialist to take ownership of our online lead generation strategy and help drive measurable business growth.

This is a hands-on role focused on managing and optimizing paid advertising campaigns, improving organic search visibility, and developing strategies for emerging AI-powered search platforms. You’ll be responsible for building campaigns, analyzing performance, identifying growth opportunities, and improving the overall return on marketing investment.

The ideal candidate combines strong Google Ads and SEO expertise with analytical thinking and a practical understanding of AI search optimization. Most importantly, you know how to turn marketing activity into qualified leads and profitable customer acquisition.

What You’ll Own

Google Ads & Paid Advertising

  • Manage and optimize Google Ads campaigns across Search, Display, Performance Max, and remarketing.
  • Conduct keyword research and improve PPC campaign structure, targeting, bidding strategies, and ad copy.
  • Optimize landing pages to improve campaign performance and conversions.
  • Monitor key metrics, including cost per lead (CPL), cost per acquisition (CPA), conversion rates, ROAS, impression share, and search terms.
  • Identify wasted advertising spend and implement improvements to campaign efficiency.

Search Engine Optimization (SEO)

  • Develop and execute organic SEO strategies to improve search visibility and generate qualified leads.
  • Manage technical, on-page, local, and off-page SEO activities.
  • Conduct keyword research and competitor analysis to identify valuable search opportunities.
  • Develop content strategies based on search intent and business priorities.
  • Improve rankings for relevant, high-value international moving and logistics searches.

AI Search Optimization (GEO / AEO)

  • Develop strategies to improve brand visibility across ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, Perplexity, and other AI-powered search platforms.
  • Improve how the company's brand and content are discovered, referenced, and recommended by AI search tools.
  • Research and test emerging Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), and LLM optimization strategies.
  • Create content strategies that support visibility across both traditional search engines and AI-powered search platforms.
  • Monitor emerging AI search trends and identify practical opportunities to improve brand visibility.

Website Optimization & Analytics

  • Collaborate with developers to improve landing pages, website structure, page speed, schema markup, and technical SEO.
  • Ensure accurate conversion tracking and attribution across marketing channels.
  • Build dashboards and reports that clearly track leads, acquisition costs, conversion rates, and marketing ROI.
  • Identify opportunities to improve website performance and conversion rates.
  • Explore new digital channels and lead-generation opportunities.
  • Use AI and automation tools to improve marketing research, content workflows, analysis, and campaign performance.

Performance Analysis & Lead Generation

  • Focus on generating qualified leads and improving profitable customer acquisition.
  • Identify which keywords, campaigns, and organic pages generate actual customer inquiries.
  • Analyze campaign spending and identify opportunities to reduce acquisition costs.
  • Evaluate competitor performance and recommend strategies to improve market visibility.
  • Use performance data to make informed marketing decisions and continuously improve results.

Required Experience & Skills

  • 3+ years of hands-on digital marketing experience.
  • Demonstrable experience managing and optimizing Google Ads campaigns.
  • Strong knowledge of PPC strategy, campaign structure, bidding, and performance optimization.
  • Hands-on experience with Google Analytics 4, Google Search Console, and Google Tag Manager.
  • Strong understanding of technical, on-page, local, and off-page SEO.
  • Experience with SEO tools such as Semrush, Ahrefs, or similar platforms.
  • Proficiency in keyword research and competitor analysis.
  • Experience with conversion tracking, attribution, landing page optimization, and conversion rate optimization (CRO).
  • Experience running lead-generation campaigns with a focus on measurable business results.
  • Familiarity with AI tools for marketing research, analysis, automation, and content creation.
  • Understanding of AI search optimization, GEO, AEO, or how brands gain visibility in generative search.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and project management skills.
  • Excellent written English communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment and manage deadlines without constant supervision.
  • Willingness to learn, test, and adapt to emerging AI marketing technologies.

Nice to Have

  • Experience marketing international moving, logistics, freight forwarding, transportation, or relocation services.
  • Experience working with other high-value service businesses.
  • Proven success improving lead quality, reducing acquisition costs, and increasing marketing ROI.
  • Experience developing SEO and paid advertising strategies for competitive markets.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You are a hands-on marketer who can build, manage, and optimize campaigns independently.
  • You focus on qualified leads and customer acquisition rather than vanity metrics such as traffic and impressions.
  • You understand how to connect marketing performance with actual business results.
  • You can identify underperforming campaigns, investigate the reasons, and take action to improve them.
  • You are analytical, proactive, and comfortable making data-driven decisions.
  • You enjoy experimenting with new AI search strategies and marketing technologies.
  • You communicate clearly, take ownership of your work, and consistently follow through.

What Success Looks Like

  • Increased volume of qualified leads from paid and organic channels.
  • Improved cost per lead and customer acquisition cost.
  • Stronger Google Ads performance and more efficient advertising spend.
  • Improved organic rankings for high-value search terms.
  • Increased brand visibility across AI-powered search platforms.
  • Accurate conversion tracking and clear marketing performance reporting.
  • Consistent improvements in lead generation and overall marketing ROI.

Interview Process

  • Initial Screening
  • Recruiter Interview
  • Client Interview
  • Offer & Onboarding

Cardinal Health’s Data Office organization empowers the enterprise with trusted, high-quality data to make informed decisions and achieve strategic goals by enabling a data-driven ecosystem where data is a strategic asset.​


The Data Management & Governance function serves as the operational backbone and quality engine of the Data Office. The team acquires, standardizes, and protects enterprise and third-party data to power clinical, commercial, and financial decisions while meeting rigorous regulatory and legal standards. Through clear guidelines, quality metrics, and policy enforcement, the team ensures enterprise data remains trusted, secure, and audit ready.


The Senior Advisor, Data Management & Governance leverages advanced clinical pharmacotherapy knowledge, regulatory acumen, and data stewardship principles to oversee enterprise pharmaceutical master data assets. This role is accountable for clinical and regulatory classifications, alternative logic, formulary alignments, and the procurement and integration of third-party data. By driving cross-functional data governance and quality frameworks, this role ensures data flowing across procurement, billing, inventory, and dispensing pipelines is clinically validated, compliant, and operationalized for decision making.


Responsibilities:

  • Establish, standardize, and govern critical clinical and product attributes across the master data lifecycle
  • Author and maintain data dictionaries, business rules, policies, standards, and validation logic to ensure data integrity during item setup, maintenance, and system conversions
  • Lead the strategic alignment of product attributes with industry-standard clinical vocabularies
  • Manage clinical, regulatory, commercial, and reimbursement inquiries and execute resolution activities
  • Resolve complex data exceptions, discrepancies, and cross-reference mapping errors
  • Evaluate regulatory changes and manufacturer notices to assess their operational, clinical, and data impact
  • Oversee the procurement, ingestion, transformation, linkage, and maintenance of third-party data and associated reference data
  • Collaborate and partner with business leaders to translate strategic objectives and business process and regulatory requirements into scalable solutions across multiple domains (e.g., CSMP, QRA, Finance, Sourcing, Revenue Management, IT, Commercial Technologies, Customer Success, and Account Management)
  • Validate external data for accuracy, completeness, and timeliness and convert unstructured data to structured data for ease of use
  • Create data views and reports that promote data quality, business insights, and enable accuracy and efficiency for downstream users
  • Lead and support data modernization initiatives
  • Subject matter expert for clinical and product datasets

Qualifications:

  • Must have an active, unrestricted Registered Pharmacist (RPh) license in good standing in at least one U.S. jurisdiction, State of Ohio, preferred
  • Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D.) or Bachelor of Science in Pharmacy (B.S. Pharm) from an accredited college of pharmacy preferred
  • 8+ years of experience in related field preferred
  • 8+ years in hospital or retail pharmacy, both preferred
  • Experience in clinical pharmacy practice, pharmacy informatics, healthcare data stewardship, or pharmaceutical supply chain master data
  • Prior experience with pharmaceutical compendia
  • Direct experience with enterprise master data management systems or ERP solutions
  • Strong understanding of healthcare and pharmaceutical coding systems
  • Proficiency using analytical tools to develop creative and innovative insights with high business value
  • Strong communication and presentation skills
  • Proven track record of translating complex clinical nuances into precise technical and operational data requirements

AlphaGov delivers public-sector consulting for cities, counties, school systems, special districts, utilities, and related agencies. Our work spans classification and compensation, organizational and operational studies, research and program evaluation, economic and workforce analysis, surveys and community research, and applied data and infrastructure research.

We engage experienced practitioners as project-based collaborators. Engagements are remote-first with occasional client travel. When you authorize it, AlphaGov may name you as an expert collaborator or key personnel on proposals that match your expertise.   • Review TRM algorithms, deemed savings values, and baseline assumptions

  • Write the engineering sections of evaluation reports and answer regulator questions
  • Contribute qualifications and past-performance narrative to AlphaGov proposals when you authorize naming

Apply to be considered.

Required

  • At least 5 years in energy engineering, energy auditing, or M&V for efficiency or electrification programs
  • Building energy modeling experience (for example eQUEST, EnergyPlus, BEopt, or similar)
  • Working knowledge of IPMVP and technical reference manuals
  • Comfortable as a 1099 project-based consultant

Nice to have

  • PE, CMVP, or CEM credential
  • Residential retrofit, weatherization, or heat pump program experience
  • Vermont, New York, or New England program experience

Job Title: Sr. Director, Digital Pricing Strategy

Job Location: Remote

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

Job Description Summary

GE HealthCare is undergoing a significant customer and business model transformation, driven by the acquisition of Intelerad and the expansion of innovative software, SaaS, and cloud-based solutions. These solutions are designed to address some of the most complex challenges in the healthcare industry.

This role is a critical leadership position supporting GE HealthCare’s transition to a SaaS-first software business model. As part of a global, cross-functional environment, the Sr. Director of Digital Pricing Strategy will define and operationalize pricing and monetization strategies across newly integrated organizations. This role will play a key part in aligning commercial, finance, and product teams while driving profitable growth and long-term scalability.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Pricing Design

Develop and lead global pricing strategies for SaaS and cloud-based offerings, ensuring alignment with overall business objectives across AI, digital, and enterprise software solutions. Drive pricing transformation as core products evolve to a cloud-first model.

SaaS Monetization & Business Model Transformation

Lead the design and implementation of modern SaaS monetization strategies, including ARR growth, net revenue retention (NRR), attach rate expansion, price realization, and margin optimization. Drive the evolution from legacy licensing models to scalable subscription, consumption, and platform-based pricing models.

Post-Acquisition Integration & Change Leadership

Partner across legacy organizations to harmonize pricing strategies, tools, and operating models following the Intelerad acquisition. Lead change management efforts to ensure adoption of new pricing frameworks and foster alignment across commercial, finance, and product teams.

Market Awareness & Competitive Intelligence

Analyze market trends, competitor pricing, and customer insights to inform pricing strategy. Stay current on industry trends, regulatory environments, and best practices in SaaS and healthcare software markets.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Collaborate closely with Sales, Finance, Product Management, Legal, Professional Services, and Marketing to ensure pricing strategies align with go-to-market objectives. Engage early in product development cycles to incorporate customer value and market needs into pricing models.

Product Pricing & Enterprise Structuring

Partner with product teams to design scalable pricing structures across multi-product portfolios. Ensure pricing models support enterprise agreements spanning multiple offerings, customer segments, and healthcare modalities.

Platform & Advanced Pricing Models

Our people at JLL are shaping the future of real estate for a better world by combining world class services, advisory and technology for our clients. We are committed to hiring the best, most talented people and empowering them to thrive, grow meaningful careers and to find a place where they belong. Whether you’ve got deep experience in commercial real estate, skilled trades or technology, or you’re looking to apply your relevant experience to a new industry, join our team as we help shape a brighter way forward.

As Senior Occupancy Planner, you will be responsible for providing strategic occupancy planning expertise, leveraging a deep understanding of our client’s space supply and demand to develop scenario and occupancy plans for our client's portfolio in a designated region.

Fostering relationships

You'll foster critical relationships between various individuals and organizations, including:

  • Corporate Real Estate to review and resolve planning forecast requirements, concerns, and issues,
  • Business Unit leadership to collect headcount forecasts and resolve headcount forecast discrepancies between their numbers and those collected at the group level,
  • Corporate Finance group to gather top-down headcount and growth projections,
  • Project management to review planning strategies that drive construction projects and support the implementation of these projects,
  • Move coordination and facility management teams to review and approve moves, develop migration plans, and conduct facility audits, and
  • Other members of the occupancy planning team to ensure the development of portfolio strategy plans across separate locations.

Driving optimal occupancy planning solutions

Your primary focus areas for this role will be managing the development of occupancy plans, sequencing group-level and individual moves, and resolving planning issues identified during client planning sessions. You will ensure the alignment of planning with corporate guidelines and that all scenarios maximize the use of space. You will recommend, educate, and enforce space policies/standards, procedures, and protocols, notify the client of customer-requested exceptions, and, as necessary, assist in developing site-specific Planning Strategies with Senior Leadership. You will be a Subject Matter Expert in the client's workplace program and in using data to drive solutions that increase productivity. You will be a leader in the Occupancy Planning and account team, modelling superior client relationship management and strategic thinking.

Reporting

One of your major requirements will be to get familiar with space utilization methods and the presentation of utilization data. Interacting with organizational leadership, you will identify space requirements and prepare and update project status reports on actual versus projected seat demand at the building level. In addition, you will report on current supply and capacity, forecast inventory changes as required, and work with the client to reconcile any discrepancies from top-down projections.

Job Description:

Investigates, analyzes, and responds to cybersecurity incidents within a network environment or enclave.

Monitors, investigates, and responds to security alerts, incidents, and suspicious activity across enterprise environments using Microsoft security technologies and other security monitoring tools.


Interprets, analyzes, and reports all events and anomalies in accordance with computer network directives, including initiating, responding to, documenting, and reporting discovered incidents.


Evaluates, tests, recommends, coordinates, monitors, and maintains cybersecurity policies, procedures, and systems, including access management for hardware, firmware, software, and cloud services.

Investigates and responds to security incidents involving unauthorized access, malware, phishing, data exfiltration, insider threats, fraud, attacks, or information leaks.

Collaborates with technical and business stakeholders to improve detection capabilities, incident response processes, and overall security operations effectiveness.

May coach and provide guidance to less-experienced professionals.

Technical Training, Certification(s), or Degree, and 5+ years of experience in cybersecurity, information security, security operations, incident response, cyber defense, or related disciplines.

About the Role

We’re looking for a detail-oriented and organized Remote Bookkeeper to support the finance team with day-to-day accounting and administrative tasks for a property management portfolio.

In this role, you’ll work primarily with AppFolio and QuickBooks Online to manage accounts payable and receivable, process payments, reconcile bank and trust accounts, maintain accurate financial records, and support month-end reporting.

You’ll handle a high volume of daily transactions and work closely with the Director of Finance, while communicating with vendors, tenants, property owners, and internal team members. The ideal candidate has bookkeeping experience, strong attention to detail, and the ability to manage financial tasks independently in a remote environment.

What You’ll Own

Accounts Payable

  • Review, code, and enter vendor invoices in AppFolio.
  • Create in-house maintenance invoices and bill tenants for tenant-caused repairs.
  • Follow up on past-due invoices and respond to vendor payment inquiries.
  • Maintain accurate vendor records, including W-9s, insurance documents, and payment methods.
  • Prepare 1099 forms.

Accounts Receivable & Tenant Ledgers

  • Post and reconcile rent receipts, deposits, and chargebacks.
  • Prepare move-out security deposit dispositions within required timelines.
  • Track overdue tenant payments and follow established collection policies.
  • Maintain accurate collections logs and tenant account records.

Bank & Trust Reconciliations

  • Reconcile operating, rent trust, and security deposit trust accounts daily.
  • Investigate and resolve outstanding items, non-sufficient funds (NSF) transactions, and unmatched payments.
  • Ensure financial transactions are accurately recorded and reconciled.

Month-End & Administrative Support

  • Generate month-end reports and gather supporting documentation for the Director of Finance.
  • Process owner distributions once approved.
  • Monitor the finance inbox and respond to or route inquiries from owners, tenants, and staff.
  • Keep owner, tenant, and vendor contact and payment information up to date.

Company Bookkeeping – QuickBooks Online

  • Record receipts and expenses for company entities.
  • Review and accurately categorize financial transactions.
  • Prepare weekly billable-hours reports.
  • Support commission and payroll data preparation.

Required Experience & Skills

  • At least 2 years of experience in bookkeeping or accounting support, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, and bank reconciliations.
  • Proficiency in AppFolio and QuickBooks Online.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets.
  • Strong data entry skills with excellent accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Excellent organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage a high volume of daily transactions.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills for working with owners, tenants, vendors, and internal teams.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment and follow established procedures.
  • High level of professionalism and commitment to confidentiality when handling financial information.

Nice to Have

  • Associate's or bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
  • Experience in property management accounting.
  • Familiarity with tenant ledgers, owner distributions, and security deposit accounting.
  • Experience maintaining vendor records and preparing 1099 forms.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You are highly organized and comfortable handling detailed, repetitive financial tasks.
  • You can manage multiple accounting priorities while maintaining accuracy.
  • You take ownership of daily responsibilities and follow established processes.
  • You proactively investigate discrepancies and follow up on unresolved transactions.
  • You communicate professionally and handle sensitive financial information with discretion.
  • You are reliable, self-motivated, and comfortable working independently in a remote setting.

What Success Looks Like

  • Vendor invoices, payments, and tenant transactions are processed accurately and on time.
  • Bank and trust accounts are reconciled daily, with discrepancies investigated promptly.
  • Tenant ledgers, vendor records, and financial information remain accurate and up to date.
  • Month-end reports and supporting documents are prepared reliably.
  • Owner distributions and other financial tasks are completed according to approval procedures.
  • The Director of Finance receives consistent and dependable bookkeeping support.

Interview Process

  • Initial Screening
  • Recruiter Interview
  • Client Interview
  • Offer & Onboarding

Job Summary:

We are seeking a motivated Automation Engineer with 3-5 years of experience to replace repetitive manual tasks across our Steady State teams (Windows, Linux, Storage, and Backup) with reliable, reusable automation. The role focuses on automating patch management across the environment using tools such as Ansible, GitLab CI/CD, HashiCorp Vault, Terraform, and the JFrog Artifactory suite (Xray, Catalog, and Curation).


Key Responsibilities:

  • Partner with Windows, Linux, storage, and backup teams to understand patch management cycles and identify opportunities to automate patching activities.
  • Analyze ServiceNow patching tickets to identify recurring manual tasks and quantify their frequency and effort across Windows, Linux, storage, and backup environments.
  • Prioritize patch management automation opportunities based on patch severity, operational risk, and impact across Windows, Linux, storage, and backup systems.
  • Develop reusable Ansible playbooks and roles to automate patch management procedures
  • Use Terraform to maintain repeatable infrastructure configurations that support patch management workflows.
  • Build and maintain GitLab CI/CD pipelines to package, test, and safely deploy patch management automation to production.
  • Manage secrets, credentials, and certificates required by automated patching workflows through HashiCorp Vault.
  • Use JFrog Artifactory, including Xray, Catalog, and Curation, to manage and secure artifacts used by patch management pipelines.
  • Validate automated patching workflows against existing manual procedures before replacing manual patching activities.
  • Track and report on patch automation coverage and reductions in manual patching effort and related ticket volume across Windows, Linux, storage, and backup systems.
  • Document patch management procedures, Ansible playbooks, and pipeline configurations for Windows, Linux, storage, and backup environments.
  • Regularly review patching ticket trends to identify recurring manual work and keep the patch automation backlog current.

You will be successful in this role if you have:

  • BA/BS degree or equivalent experience and 3-5 years of experience in infrastructure operations, patch management, or related engineering roles, including patching automation.
  • Hands-on experience using Ansible, Terraform, GitLab CI/CD, and HashiCorp Vault to support production patch management workflows.
  • Experience analyzing patching tickets and incident data in ServiceNow or a similar ITSM tool to identify recurring issues and opportunities to improve patch delivery.
  • Ability to gather patching requirements from operations teams and translate patch cycles and procedures into repeatable workflows.
  • Working knowledge of Windows and Linux systems administration, storage, and backup operations, with experience supporting patch management across these environments.
  • Strong scripting skills in Bash, Python, PowerShell, or similar languages to automate patching tasks and validation.

Overview

Are you ready to take your career to the next level? LoanCare, one of the top providers in the mortgage services industry, seeks an individual with a solid work history in the mortgage or real estate industry, to join our team as a Senior Counsel - Litigation. ­­­The ideal candidate will enjoy working with clients, both internal and external, be detail oriented, and is driven to meet tight deadlines in a fast-paced environment. If you are ready for a career and not just your next job, now is the time to join our team and become a part of something big

Responsibilities

  • Responsible for overseeing and managing Litigation related to our GSE loans from defaulted issuers, by supervising, coordinating and strategizing with outside counsel in connection with lawsuits and claims and providing complete transparency to the account owning GSE
  • Advise senior executives on litigation strategies
  • Supervise the work of other junior attorneys and paralegals
  • Lead negotiations and revisions of renewing subservicing agreements with clients
  • Manage all aspects of consumer finance litigation, including the selection and management of, and communication with outside counsel and administration and processing of outside counsel’s legal billing
  • Lead presentations regarding periodic updates and risk reports to senior litigation counsel
  • Provide legal advice to managers and supervisors and perform necessary research for guidance in operational processes and procedures
  • Manage and oversee the responses to discovery requests, including e-discovery
  • Review and provide guidance on subpoena duces tecum
  • Assist internal business units with responses to information requests from external LoanCare clients
  • Identify trends in litigation matters as well as borrower and/or regulatory complaints; communicating these trends to senior litigation counsel as well as internal business units; coordinating with operations in order to develop policies and procedures to remediate issues
  • Provide support and assistance to Senior In-house counsel in responding to requests for legal advice and related assistance from internal business unit
  • All other duties as assigned

Qualifications

  • Juris Doctor from an ABA accredited law school and state bar admission required
  • 7+ years of experience in consumer/mortgage loan servicing litigation defense management
  • Knowledge of mortgage origination, closing and servicing practices
  • Knowledge of various types of mortgage loan products such as conventional, ARMs, HELOC, etc.
  • Knowledge of loan documents (note, mortgage/deed of trust, etc.)
  • Knowledge of Federal and State Consumer Finance Laws as well as Government Sponsored Entity Seller/Servicer Guidelines
  • Knowledge of federal laws and regulations governing residential mortgages, including ECOA, FCRA, TILA, RESPA, and FDCPA and the ability to apply the requirements to business practices
  • Experience in representing mortgage servicers against ‘consumer’ litigation claims involving such matters as privacy, contested foreclosures, FDCPA, FCRA, TILA, RESPA and other disputes under state and federal consumer protection laws
  • Experience overseeing complex litigation
  • Experience responding to discovery requests, including e-discovery
  • Experience researching, interpreting, and articulating legal issues
  • Experience working directly with management on residential mortgage default litigation issues
  • Substantial experience delivering presentations to clients and executive management
  • Strong legal research ability and familiarity with legal research tools (Westlaw or Lexis Nexis)
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Ability to maintain confidential and/or privileged information
  • Ability to work independently, as well as, a team setting
  • Ability to interpret and apply applicable laws and regulations
  • Flexibility to simultaneously manage a wide range of projects and matters and meet deadlines in a changing and fast-paced environment
  • Results driven, has an attention to detail and passion for driving best practices

Total Rewards

LoanCare’s Total Rewards Package offers a comprehensive blend of health and welfare, financial, lifestyle and learning benefits to support employee well-being and engagement. Highlights include:

  • Health & Welfare Coverage: Optional medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance

  • Retirement & Investment: Fidelity National Financial matching 401(k) and employee stock purchase plans
  • Wellness Programs: Access to mental health resources, including free Calm memberships, and initiatives that promote physical and emotional well-being

      <title>Current: Freelance Marketo Email Engineer</title>
      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Front-End Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Remote (US)
</p>

<h3>&nbsp;</h3>
<h2><strong>About the Role</strong></h2>
<p>As a Freelance Marketo Email Specialist, you'll build, test, and launch email programs in Marketo for a range of client brands. This is a hands-on, execution-only contract role with no leadership or management responsibilities. You'll take approved briefs and turn them into working programs, building responsive templates and modules, setting up smart lists and flows, and making sure every send goes out right the first time. You know Marketo well enough to spot a broken token, a misfired trigger, or a segmentation gap before it reaches a subscriber. You'll take direction from our internal team, get up to speed fast, and deliver accurate builds on schedule with minimal oversight.</p>
<h2><strong>Key Responsibilities</strong></h2>
<ul>
<li>Build and launch email programs in Marketo, including one-off sends, nurture streams, engagement programs, and triggered campaigns.</li>
<li>Develop and maintain responsive email templates and modular components in HTML and CSS, using Marketo's template syntax, variables, and editable sections.</li>
<li>Set up smart lists, smart campaigns, flow steps, and segmentations that match the targeting and logic in the brief.</li>
<li>Use tokens, dynamic content, and snippets to personalize emails and keep programs easy to clone and reuse.</li>
<li>QA every email before launch: rendering across clients and devices (e.g. Litmus or Email on Acid), links, tokens, personalization fallbacks, and list logic.</li>
<li>Manage program structure, naming conventions, and folder organization so client instances stay clean and easy to navigate.</li>
<li>Build to the brief and requirements provided, and flag any gaps or errors in the request before they become problems in the send.</li>
<li>Communicate status, timelines, and blockers clearly with your internal point of contact.</li>
<li>Document builds and processes so other team members can pick up, update, or reuse the work.</li>
<li>Follow established Marketo, deliverability, and accessibility standards on every build.</li>
</ul>
<h2><strong>Qualifications</strong></h2>
<h3><strong>Required</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li>At least 3 years of hands-on experience building and deploying email campaigns in Marketo Engage.</li>
<li>Strong working knowledge of Marketo programs, smart lists, smart campaigns, tokens, snippets, and dynamic content.</li>
<li>Proficiency in HTML and CSS for email, including responsive and hybrid coding and Marketo template syntax.</li>
<li>Experience with email rendering and QA tools such as Litmus or Email on Acid.</li>
<li>A detail-oriented QA process that catches errors in logic, links, and personalization before launch.</li>
<li>Experience working across multiple clients or Marketo instances, adapting quickly to different setups and conventions.</li>
<li>Clear, proactive communication, including flagging risks early and giving accurate time estimates.</li>
<li>Ability to work independently, take direction well, and hit deadlines across overlapping requests.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong>Preferred</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li>Marketo Certified Expert or Marketo Certified Associate.</li>
<li>Familiarity with email deliverability, authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), and list hygiene.</li>
<li>Experience with email accessibility standards (e.g. WCAG).</li>
<li>Experience with lead scoring, lifecycle programs, and Marketo–Salesforce CRM sync.</li>
<li>Experience with other marketing automation platforms (e.g. Salesforce Marketing Cloud, HubSpot, Braze).</li>
<li>Agency or consulting experience.</li>
</ul>
<h2><strong>Why Current</strong></h2>
<p>At Current, we believe the best digital work happens when strategy, design, production, and technology operate as one team. We partner with ambitious brands to create digital experiences that are thoughtful, scalable, and built to drive real impact.</p>
<p>We're a remote-first agency with teams across the US, working collaboratively across websites, platforms, campaigns, CRM ecosystems, and digital product experiences. Our environment is fast-paced, highly collaborative, and built for people who enjoy solving complex technical challenges alongside smart, supportive teammates.</p>
<p>You'll have the opportunity to work across a variety of clients and technologies, and contribute to meaningful digital experiences within a growing agency environment.</p>
<p>This is a freelance, contract engagement. The target hourly rate for this role is $50 - $70 per hour. Actual rate is influenced by a wide array of factors, including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, and location.</p>

<p><strong>To apply:</strong> <a href="https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/current-freelance-marketo-email-engineer">https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/current-freelance-marketo-email-engineer</a></p>
</description>

      <title>Clover Health: Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations</title>
      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Full-Stack Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Remote - USA
</p>

<p>Clover Health is investing in our fraud detection and investigation capabilities and is seeking a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention &amp; Investigations to join our Legal department as a senior individual contributor. This hybrid role combines: (1) managing hands-on investigations of potential provider fraud with (2) building AI-powered tools and processes to make investigations more efficient and help catch potential future fraud earlier. You will develop and pilot new AI-enabled investigatory processes for Clover’s Medicare Advantage business, and own resulting investigations, in collaboration with Clover’s Special Investigations Unit (SIU) and other stakeholders.</p>
<p>This is a non-attorney role.&nbsp; You will work hand-in-hand with Clover’s lawyers and SIU to ensure that new investigatory processes you develop, and the resulting investigations, comply with Clover policies and regulatory requirements. Success in this role requires someone sharp, creative, and technically hands-on—someone who does not just use existing analytics tools but builds their own. That might mean writing a script to automate repetitive work, pulling apart a dataset when a standard report falls short, or working with an LLM until it produces something genuinely useful—all with the goal of finding smarter, more effective ways to investigate potential provider fraud.</p>
<p><strong>As a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention &amp; Investigations, you will:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Build Your Own Investigative Tooling: </strong>Use AI to write the queries, scripts, and prompts that turn millions of claim lines and/or medical record data into a prioritized list of leads. Prototype detection logic yourself rather than waiting on a roadmap, and hand off what works to data science and engineering to productionize. We expect you to be the person who builds v1.</li>
<li><strong>Investigate Potential Fraud End-to-End With AI in the Loop: </strong>Own a portfolio of fraud investigations sourced using the tooling you develop, in collaboration with Clover’s SIU. Develop investigative plans, gather and analyze evidence (including claims data and medical records), and reach well-supported conclusions.&nbsp; Use LLMs and analytics to compress the parts of an investigation that have always been slow — reading unstructured data, triaging grievance narratives, and sizing exposure.&nbsp;</li>
<li><strong>Build Defensible Documentation: </strong>Develop case files and memos that are factually complete, well-organized, and prepared with the evidentiary and procedural standards necessary for downstream enforcement, recoveries, or provider actions.</li>
<li><strong>Collaborate Across Functions: </strong>Work with Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, provider relations, revenue operations, and SIU teams to gather information, validate findings, and translate investigative outcomes into operational improvements, provider education, and member impact.</li>
<li><strong>Communicate Findings Clearly: </strong>Prepare concise written reports and oral briefings that translate complex investigative facts into clear narratives for senior leadership and other stakeholders.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Success in this role looks like:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>In your first 90 days</strong>, you have embedded yourself as a trusted partner to both the Legal department and Clover’s SIU. You have built working relationships with key stakeholders across Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, revenue operations, and legal teams, and you have begun working through your initial portfolio of fraud investigations and ad hoc referrals.</li>
<li><strong>By 6 months</strong>, you are independently managing a steady caseload of fraud investigations with consistently high-quality work product, in collaboration with SIU. You have a clear working rhythm with Legal and SIU, and you have built at least one working tool — a script, a notebook, a dashboard, a prompt.</li>
<li><strong>By 12 months</strong>, you have a track record of strong investigations, successful recoveries and/or referrals, and effective cross-functional collaboration. Senior leaders across Clover view you as a trusted person to call when they have a hunch that something doesn't look right and want it examined.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>You should get in touch if:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Knowledge of healthcare fraud schemes &amp; investigative experience: </strong>You have experience in healthcare fraud investigations, program integrity, or SIU operations, ideally within Medicare Advantage or managed care.&nbsp; You understand healthcare fraud schemes and know how to use claims data, medical records, and provider documentation to build a defensible factual record.</li>
<li><strong>You are AI-native and enjoy building things using LLMs:</strong> You can use LLMs to write SQL, Python, etc., to interrogate large claims and/or medical record datasets, automate investigative work, and prototype your own solutions rather than waiting for someone else to build them. <em>We do not expect production-grade engineering or require formal technical training—we value demonstrated ability to build, ship, and showcase solutions that work.</em></li>
<li><strong>Strong communication skills: </strong>You are a strong writer and communicator who can turn complex investigative findings into clear memos, referrals, and executive summaries, and you are comfortable building in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Bonus points if:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>
<ul>

<div class="content-intro"><p>Lithic is the modern card issuing and processing platform empowering ambitious financial companies to build the future of payments.</p>
<p>Our infrastructure powers card programs for 100+ innovative clients, from fintechs reimagining credit and digital banking to platforms transforming disbursements and spend management. Companies like Mercury, Flex, and Novo rely on Lithic's developer-friendly APIs, direct network connections, and flawless reconciliation to launch and scale card programs in weeks, not years.</p>
<p>We're building a future where access to better financial products materially improves people's lives, free from the constraints of 30-year-old mainframes and legacy processors. We're proud to be backed by world-class investors who share that vision, including Bessemer Venture Partners, Index Ventures, Spark Capital, Stripes, and Mastercard, along with many others.&nbsp;</p>
<p>We're a team of 170+ across 26 states and 7 countries, headquartered in New York City.&nbsp;</p></div><p>We are hiring a <strong>Senior Software Engineer</strong> for the Product Platform team, which owns the foundational layer of our API that all other Lithic products build on top. The team’s mission is to make Lithic's API the best in fintech — reliable, consistent, and a joy to integrate with. This includes API Gateway, Events Platform, API key management and authorization, audit logging, or API norms and versioning strategy.</p>

<li>Comfort with designing systems from scratch and owning the product development process end-to-end</li>

<p>The annual US salary range for this role is $160,000 to $200,000 plus equity. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Lithic and will be narrowed during the interview process based on the candidate’s experience and qualifications.&nbsp;</p>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> New York City, Remote
</p>

<h2>Alloy is where you belong!</h2>
<p>Alloy is the AI-powered identity and fraud prevention platform that accelerates onboarding, stops fraud, and scales compliance across the customer lifecycle so financial organizations can grow without limits. More than 900 of the world's leading financial institutions and fintechs trust Alloy for smarter risk management that drives growth.<br><br>Through our values: Be Bold, Go Fast, Collaborate, and Celebrate Our Differences, we are creating a workplace where you can grow, thrive, and belong. See how we’ve been continuously recognized and named one of <a href="https://www.inc.com/profile/alloy_ny">Inc. Magazine’s Best Workplaces</a>, <a href="https://www.forbes.com/companies/alloy/?list=americas-best-startup-employers&amp;sh=55c076453c61">Forbes America’s Best Startup Employers</a>, <a href="https://www.americanbanker.com/list/best-places-to-work-in-fintech-2022">Best Fintech to Work for by American Banker</a>, year after year.<br><br>Check out our investors and read more about us <a href="https://www.alloy.com/about">here</a>.</p>
<h2>About the team</h2>
<p>We're standing up a new function at Alloy: Forward Deployed Engineering. Our largest enterprise customers need a trusted technical partner with a strong point of view on how Alloy fits into their tech stack and fraud strategy. As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll be that partner - embedded with our most strategic accounts and owning the technical outcome end-to-end, with each deployment becoming the foundation for the next.</p>
<p>You'll be one of the first two engineers on this founding team. This is a software engineering role through and through - based within our Engineering org, with a scope that spans software, product, and solutions engineering. You won't just join this function - you'll define how it works.</p>
<p>Alloy operates in a hybrid-work environment. We look to foster collaboration and community by having our local employees onsite three days a week.</p>
<h2><strong>What you'll be doing</strong></h2>
<ul>
<li>Architect and tune customer and channel-partner deployments end-to-end — API integrations, third-party data integrations, SDKs, and latency constraints.</li>
<li>Write production code across our stack: TypeScript, JavaScript (ES6/React), Python (Django), Node.js, PostgreSQL, OpenSearch, and AWS.</li>
<li>Serve as Alloy's credible technical voice with customer engineering leadership, making architectural calls in real time.</li>
<li>Own the engineering track of QBRs for your accounts and serve in their on-call escalation path.</li>
<li>Turn your work into reusable platform primitives and docs, so each deployment makes the next one faster.</li>
</ul>
<h2><strong>Who we’re looking for</strong></h2>
<ul>
<li>5+ years of hands-on experience developing production-ready software, with a proven track record of delivering robust, scalable solutions.</li>
<li>Experience in a customer-facing technical role, Forward Deployed Engineering, solutions engineering with deep technical ownership, or similar - where you were accountable to an external stakeholder, not just an internal roadmap.</li>
<li>Strong backend and API fluency, with the ability to read and write production code across services you don't own.</li>
<li>Sound architectural judgment under ambiguity: you can make and defend technical decisions in the room, with a customer watching.</li>
<li>A genuine pull toward customer-facing work - you find energy in solving a real customer's real problem, alongside their engineers.</li>
<li>A clear technical communicator who can explain a complex integration tradeoff to a bank's VP of Engineering and to an Alloy PM in the same afternoon.</li>
<li>Ability to travel on occasion to our NYC office, as well as client offices in the US.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Nice to have:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Experience at a company with a strong Forward Deployed Engineering culture (Palantir, Scale AI, Ramp, Plaid, Stripe, etc.).</li>
<li>Familiarity with identity, fraud, KYC/KYB, or financial services infrastructure.</li>
<li>Experience with SDK development or embedded front-end integrations.</li>
</ul>
<p>We're a lean team, so your impact will be felt immediately, and opportunities will grow as the company scales up. If this all sounds like a good fit for you, why not join us?</p>
<p>Alloy is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. Below is the anticipated starting base compensation range for this role; however, pay may vary depending on job-related knowledge, in-demand skills, relevant experience, and/or geography. In addition to a competitive base salary, this position is also eligible for equity awards in the form of stock options (ISOs) as well as a competitive total benefits package. Your recruiter will be happy to walk you through the details and what compensation could look like for you specifically!</p>
<p><em>This position has a salary range of $141,000 to $250,000.&nbsp;</em></p>
<h2>Benefits and Perks&nbsp;</h2>
<ul>
<li>Unlimited PTO and flexible work policy</li>
<li>Employee stock options</li>
<li>Medical, dental, vision plans with HSA (monthly employer contribution) and FSA options</li>
<li>401k with 100% match up to 4% of annual employee compensation&nbsp;</li>
<li>Eligible new parents receive 16 weeks of paid parental leave&nbsp;</li>
<li>Home office stipend for new employees</li>
<li>Annual Learning &amp; Development annual stipend</li>
<li>Well-being benefits include access to ClassPass, OneMedical, UrbanSitter, and Spring Health&nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>Apply right here! You've found the application!</p>

We encourage applicants to share needed accommodations with their recruiter.</p>
<p>All Alloy jobs are listed on our careers page. Any communication during the recruitment process, including interview requests or job offers, will come directly from a recruiting team member with an <a href="http://alloy.com/">alloy.com</a> email address. We do not use outside applications or automated text messaging in our recruiting process. We will not ask for any sensitive financial or identification information during the recruiting process. If you’re ever unsure, please contact us directly via our website before sharing personal information.</p>
